chunks: And from him, from Al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Musa, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The slave man does not combine (in marriage) from women more than two free women.
ai.seo_question: What is the maximum number of wives a male slave can have in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the marital capacity of a male slave (abd), limiting him to two free women (hurra), which contrasts with the general permission for free men to have up to four wives. Scholars note this restriction reflects the economic and social constraints placed upon slaves, ensuring that their marital obligations remain manageable within their specific legal status. The ruling underscores the nuanced application of Islamic family law, where social hierarchy directly influences personal status rights.
